Sedno — Account deletion

Version: 23 October 2026

Request account deletion by email

Controller and contact

Controller: Mariusz Bąbka, an individual, ul. Słowiańska 91, Modlniczka, Poland. For privacy and account deletion, contact contact@sedno.xyz. The controller has not appointed a data protection officer.

This policy covers the Sedno app and support for its users. Poland is the first selected market. The app is for people aged 13 and over. People aged 13–17 should use it with permission from a parent or guardian. The app does not check your age or collect your date of birth.

The full Polish privacy policy is available at https://sedno.xyz/prywatnosc/ and in the app. This English version is available in the app. A short Polish summary is at https://sedno.xyz/#prywatnosc. Account deletion instructions in Polish are at https://sedno.xyz/usun-konto. The server has been running since 19 October 2026.

Deleting your account and data

We will delete your Sedno account, its data on the server and local history on this device. This cannot be undone. Deleting your account does not cancel your subscription. To stop charges, open Google Play → Payments and subscriptions → Subscriptions → Sedno → Cancel subscription.

In the app, choose Account → Delete account → Delete account and data. After successful deletion, we remove your Sedno identity in Firebase, account sessions, linked installations, request metadata and purchase records from the Sedno database. We do not delete your Google account.

Without the app, email contact@sedno.xyz with the subject “Sedno account deletion”. Provide the email address you use to sign in. Do not send passwords, sign-in codes, tokens, identity documents, photos or texts to simplify or correct. Sending the email alone does not delete your account. We will confirm that you control the account before deleting it. If there is doubt, we will ask only for extra information needed for verification.

Deleting your account by email or on another device does not remove history on your other devices. Delete it in History or clear app data in Android settings. We have no remote access to local history. Purchases and data retained by Google are subject to Google's policies.

Retention in the app and Sedno database

Text and results on the Sedno server: content is not saved; it is used in memory to handle your request. Local history: 7 days, with cleanup as described above. Request metadata and HMAC text fingerprints older than 8 days are removed by a separate hourly job, regardless of app traffic. Daily usage counters and quota reservations are retained for up to 8 days.

Account sessions are valid for 7 days and guest sessions for 90 days. The same hourly job deletes expired sessions. An expired session does not allow access, even before its record is physically deleted. An unlinked guest identity older than 90 days is deleted once it has no sessions or requests left. This may happen later than day 90.

Accounts, linked installations and Sedno purchase records are retained until account deletion. The current app does not automatically delete inactive accounts or expired purchase records. Technical Google Play notification identifiers currently have no automatic deletion deadline. They do not contain purchase tokens or account links. We do not claim retention periods that have not been implemented.

Selected operational retention rules

For production, we adopt these rules: technical logs and database backups up to 30 days; correspondence up to 90 days after a case closes; minimal confirmation of handling data rights up to 12 months after closure. Confirmation retains only the date, request type and outcome, without full correspondence. These are organisational rules. The main log store is set to 30 days. Backups of the previous SQL database do not cover Firestore. New backups and recovery need separate configuration; we do not claim they are automatically enabled. If enabled, the 30-day maximum applies. Other stores, exports and email handling rules need separate checks and implementation before public release.

Backups are for disaster recovery, not ongoing use of deleted accounts. After restoration, deletions must be applied again before data is made available. For a specific legal obligation or dispute, only necessary data may be retained for the period required by that obligation or case. We do not extend all retention unnecessarily.

Sedno's retention periods do not change provider periods. Firebase describes retaining sign-in IP addresses for several weeks and other authentication data until user deletion is requested; subsequent deletion from active systems and backups may take up to 180 days. OpenAI retention is described in the AI section. Google payment data and metrics follow the relevant service policies.

Your rights and contact

To the extent provided by the GDPR, you may request access to and a copy of your data, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and portability of relevant data. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests. If processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it without affecting earlier processing. Rights are subject to legal conditions and exceptions.

Email contact@sedno.xyz. We respond without undue delay, normally within one month of receiving your request. In cases allowed by the GDPR, this may be extended by two months; we will explain why within the first month. If there is reasonable doubt about your identity, we will ask for necessary confirmation without routinely requesting an identity document.

You can complain to the President of the Polish Personal Data Protection Office: https://uodo.gov.pl. A general message about your data does not require you to provide texts you simplify or correct.
